paths.title: Origins of the Force traditions
units: Exar Kun and the Great Sith War

readings.title: Je'daii and Tython
readings.body: Dawn of the Jedi depicts an ancient order on Tython seeking balance between light and dark. This Legends account must not be treated as the established origin of the Canon Jedi.
readings.question: Compare balance as an institutional ideal with balance as a personal practice.
readings.source: Dawn of the Jedi: Force Storm

readings.title: Early Jedi schisms
readings.body: Legends accounts describe disagreements over the permissible uses of the Force and the emergence of rival traditions. Different stories cover different conflicts; a single simplified origin story obscures these distinctions.
readings.question: How can institutions preserve disagreement without encouraging coercion?
readings.source: The Essential Guide to the Force

readings.title: Ancient Sith civilization
readings.body: Tales of the Jedi portrays a Sith civilization with its own history, hierarchy and traditions. The word Sith can refer to a people or an order depending on the historical context.
readings.question: Explain why distinguishing ethnicity from institutional membership matters.
readings.source: Tales of the Jedi: The Golden Age of the Sith

readings.title: Great Hyperspace War
readings.body: The Golden Age of the Sith and Fall of the Sith Empire portray a succession struggle and conflict between the ancient Sith Empire and Republic. Read these as Legends narratives rather than Canon chronology.
readings.question: How can competition for leadership undermine collective goals?
readings.source: Tales of the Jedi: The Fall of the Sith Empire

readings.title: Exar Kun and the Great Sith War
readings.body: Exar Kun's transformation and alliance with Ulic Qel-Droma illustrate ambition, manipulation and the consequences of pursuing forbidden knowledge in Legends.
readings.question: Distinguish intellectual curiosity from entitlement to power.
readings.source: Tales of the Jedi: Dark Lords of the Sith; The Sith War

readings.title: Mandalorian Wars
readings.body: The Knights of the Old Republic games portray disagreement over Jedi intervention in the Mandalorian Wars. Revan's decision to fight is central to later conflicts.
readings.question: Compare the risks of intervention and nonintervention without assuming either is always right.
readings.source: Knights of the Old Republic; Knights of the Old Republic II

readings.title: Revan and Malak
readings.body: The first game explores former Jedi leaders who become Sith and a protagonist whose identity is revealed through the story. Player choices complicate claims about a single narrative outcome.
readings.question: What is the relationship between memory, responsibility and identity?

readings.title: Jedi Civil War
readings.body: The conflict between Revan and Malak's Sith forces and the Republic provides a setting for examining loyalty, institutional fracture and redemption.
readings.question: How does a movement change when its leaders prioritize victory over its original purpose?

readings.title: Kreia and the Jedi Exile
readings.body: Kreia challenges both Jedi and Sith assumptions and questions dependence on the Force. Her claims are a character's perspective, not necessarily the game's final philosophical verdict.
readings.question: Identify a persuasive claim and a counterargument to it.
readings.source: Knights of the Old Republic II: The Sith Lords

readings.title: Vitiate and the Sith Empire
readings.body: The Old Republic depicts a long-lived Sith Emperor and a renewed imperial state. Its narratives examine competing loyalties and the consequences of concentrated authority.
readings.question: Compare personal power with institutional resilience.

readings.title: Living and Cosmic Force
readings.body: The Clone Wars season six explores the relationship between living beings and a larger Force through Yoda's journey.
readings.question: How does a fictional cosmology differ from an empirical claim?

readings.title: Mortis
readings.body: The Clone Wars Mortis arc depicts the Father, Son and Daughter as mysterious beings associated with balance and opposing aspects of the Force.
readings.question: Compare symbolic and literal interpretations of the arc.

readings.title: Vergences
readings.body: The Phantom Menace uses the concept of a vergence in connection with Anakin. Other stories associate unusual Force phenomena with places.
readings.question: What evidence would distinguish a narrative interpretation from speculation?

readings.title: World Between Worlds
readings.body: Rebels depicts Ezra entering a mysterious realm connecting moments in time. Its limits should not be inferred from fan theories alone.
readings.question: Identify what the episode demonstrates versus what it leaves unresolved.

readings.title: Force spirits
readings.body: The original trilogy and The Clone Wars depict continued identity after death for certain characters.
readings.question: Compare the fictional motif with differing philosophical accounts of personal identity.

readings.title: Stoic agency
readings.body: Epictetus distinguishes what depends on our judgment and choice from external outcomes. This is not a demand to suppress emotion or ignore injustice.
readings.question: Separate a current concern into choices you can make and outcomes you cannot guarantee.

readings.title: Buddhist impermanence
readings.body: Buddhist traditions teach impermanence and examine how clinging contributes to suffering. Interpretations vary across schools; nonattachment is not indifference.
readings.question: Describe a changing experience without assuming it defines your permanent identity.

readings.title: Daoist noncoercive action
readings.body: Wu wei is often interpreted as action without excessive forcing. Daoist texts use paradox and imagery rather than prescribing one universal technique.
readings.question: Identify a situation where less interference could improve an outcome.

readings.title: Nietzschean self-overcoming
readings.body: Nietzsche examines self-transformation, inherited values and the creation of meaning. His account of power is disputed and cannot be reduced to domination.
readings.question: Identify an inherited assumption and evaluate whether it serves your considered values.
readings.source: Nietzsche, Thus Spoke Zarathustra; Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy: Nietzsche

readings.title: Ancient theories of soul
readings.body: Plato and Aristotle offer different accounts of soul, life and human capacities. Their concepts are not interchangeable with fictional Force metaphysics.
readings.question: Compare two accounts of personal identity and state what each leaves unexplained.

paths.title: Seven classical lightsaber forms
units: Shien and Djem So: counteroffensive philosophy
Juyo and Vaapad: intensity and distinctions

readings.title: Shii-Cho
readings.body: Form I is traditionally presented as foundational in expanded lore. Study how a shared vocabulary supports later specialization.
readings.question: Why does foundational training remain useful after specialization?

readings.title: Makashi
readings.body: Form II emphasizes dueling in fictional descriptions; Count Dooku is a prominent associated practitioner.
readings.question: Compare precision with adaptability as intellectual virtues.

readings.title: Soresu
readings.body: Form III emphasizes defense; Obi-Wan is commonly associated with it.
readings.question: When is restraint more effective than immediate response?

readings.title: Ataru
readings.body: Form IV is associated with acrobatic movement, notably Yoda in fictional depictions.
readings.question: How do environmental constraints affect a chosen strategy?

readings.title: Shien and Djem So
readings.body: Form V includes distinct variants associated with responding to opposition; avoid treating the variants as identical.
readings.question: Distinguish responding to criticism from escalating conflict.

readings.title: Niman
readings.body: Form VI is commonly described as integrating elements of other forms.
readings.question: What are the benefits and limitations of broad competence?

readings.title: Juyo and Vaapad
readings.body: Form VII includes Juyo and the distinct Vaapad variant associated with Mace Windu in expanded lore.
readings.question: Distinguish emotional awareness from emotional control.
